newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Pressure mounts on Serbs over Bosnia polls.
newsitem.headline: Pressure mounts on Serbs over Bosnia polls.

text.p: The Bosnian Serbs faced mounting pressure on Saturday to participate in local elections after the international community issued a warning that security fears put the polls "at substantial risk".
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel arrived in Sarajevo to join U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum for a series of crisis talks with leaders of all three Bosnian factions.
They were holding meetings with Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic and fellow presidency members Kresimir Zubak, a Croat, and Momcilo Krajisnik, a Serb, officials said.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), facing threats from the Bosnian Serbs to pull out of the municipal elections set for November 23 and 24, issued an urgent appeal for restraint, saying: "All sides must cool it."
OSCE spokesman David Foley said decisions on whether to proceed must be taken immediately. "The time is now," he told a news conference.

Postponement of the municipal elections, which follow September 14 elections for a presidency and parliament, would be a major blow to the Bosnian peace process and to the prestige of the international community.

The OSCE mission head in Bosnia, Robert Frowick of the United States, has been holding urgent talks with the Bosnian Serb leadership to try to persuade them to take a full part in the electoral process.
Kornblum on Friday held last ditch talks with Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic.
Plavsic said earlier this week that the Serbs might hold their own local elections without OSCE supervision.
Then on Friday she said a security crisis surrounding the resettlement of Moslems in Serb areas made it "almost impossible" for the Serbs to participate in the elections.

The resettlement of Moslem villagers in Serb areas of northern Bosnia has stoked up tension, with Serbs arresting Moslems for possession of arms and Moslems accusing Serbs of blowing up houses they want to occupy.
Foley called for an end to "gamesmanship and brinkmanship", saying the elections were a crucial part of the peace process.
"There are significant fears that if the current security situation were to continue from now to the municipal elections, they would be put substantially at risk," he said.

Putting off the elections would pose a major security headache. NATO is set to begin a rapid withdrawal of its 58,000 peacekeepers after the November polling date, with the drawdown expected to be complete in January.
The international community has been putting pressure on the Serbs to participate in the polls, threatening to exclude them from financial aid for post-war reconstruction.
